items.title: Lobachevsky function
items.statement:
For real $\theta$, define the Lobachevsky function
$$
\Lambda(\theta)=-\int_0^\theta \log|2\sin u|\,du,
$$
where the integral is interpreted improperly at zeros of $\sin u$.

references.title: Jessica S. Purcell, Hyperbolic Knot Theory
references.locator: Definition 9.2, printed p.174

items.title: Ideal tetrahedron shape and cusp holonomy
items.statement:
Use the upper half-space model
$$\mathbb H^3=\{(x+iy,t):x,y\in\mathbb R,\ t>0\},\qquad ds^2=t^{-2}(dx^2+dy^2+dt^2),$$
whose ideal boundary is $\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$. An oriented ideal tetrahedron in normalized position has ideal vertices $0,1,\infty,z$, where $\operatorname{Im}z>0$. Its three edge-shape parameters are
$$z,\qquad z'=\frac1{1-z},\qquad z''=\frac{z-1}{z},$$
each assigned to one pair of opposite edges; the parameter at a corner of a truncated ideal vertex triangle is the parameter of the incident edge. For an oriented path $\gamma$ in a triangulated torus link of ideal vertices, its cusp multiplier $H(\gamma)$ is the product of the corner parameters encountered along $\gamma$, using the parameter when the path cuts off that corner on its left and its reciprocal when it cuts off the corner on its right.

references.title: Jessica S. Purcell, Hyperbolic Knot Theory

items.title: Essential torus curves with the same primitive class are isotopic
items.statement: Let $T$ be a torus. Every essential smoothly embedded simple closed curve $c\subset T$ represents a primitive element of $H_1(T;\mathbb Z)$. If $c,d\subset T$ are essential smoothly embedded simple closed curves with $[c]=\pm[d]$, then they are ambient isotopic in $T$. If they are also disjoint and distinct, they cobound an embedded annulus in $T$.

items.title: Rank-two Kleinian subgroups give proper embedded horocusps

references.title: Michael Kapovich, Hyperbolic Manifolds and Discrete Groups
references.locator: Sections 4.6 and 4.12–4.13, discrete groups and cusp geometry; the rank-two and Shimizu matrix arguments required here are supplied explicitly

items.statement:
Assume AC. Use the upper half-space model $\mathbb H^3=\{(z,y):z\in\mathbb C,y>0\}$ with metric $(|dz|^2+dy^2)/y^2$. Let $\Gamma\le\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb C)$ be discrete and torsion-free, and suppose that it contains a subgroup $A\cong\mathbb Z^2$. Then $A$ fixes a unique ideal point. After conjugating that point to infinity, its full stabilizer $P=\operatorname{Stab}_\Gamma(\infty)$ consists of translations by a lattice $\Lambda\le\mathbb C$ of rank two. It is the unique maximal abelian subgroup containing $A$.

For a sufficiently large $R$, the quotient of the closed horoball $\{y\ge R\}$ by $P$ embeds properly in $M=\Gamma\backslash\mathbb H^3$. Its boundary is a compact torus, its interior is a cusp, and its volume is $\operatorname{area}(\mathbb C/\Lambda)/(2R^2)$. If $M$ has exactly one topological end, the complement of the open cusp has compact closure.

No finite-volume thin decomposition, abstract peripheral recognition, or rigidity theorem is assumed or concluded here. The rank-two subgroup and the quotient presentation of $M$ are hypotheses.
items.axiom_use: Full AC is retained for the metric and covering interfaces; the matrix and cusp arguments use only finite choices and sequences.

items.title: A quasiconformal conjugacy of finite-covolume Kleinian groups is Möbius

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G=\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb C)$ act on the Riemann sphere by Möbius transformations. Let $\Gamma\le G$ be discrete, with finite nonzero Haar quotient measure $\nu$ on $X=\Gamma\backslash G$. Here Haar quotient measure means the right invariant Radon measure obtained by locally transporting Haar measure through the covering projection $G\to X$; its normalization is immaterial. Let $\theta:\Gamma\to G$ be a homomorphism, and let $h:\widehat{\mathbb C}\to\widehat{\mathbb C}$ be an orientation-preserving quasiconformal homeomorphism satisfying $h\circ\gamma=\theta(\gamma)\circ h$ for every $\gamma\in\Gamma$. Then $h$ is Möbius.

This statement assumes the existence of the quasiconformal boundary conjugacy. It does not assert that an abstract group isomorphism or a quasi-isometry produces one.

items.title: Uniform circular distortion gives planar quasiconformality by difference quotients

references.title: F. W. Gehring, Definitions for a Class of Plane Quasiconformal Mappings

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $h:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ be an orientation-preserving homeomorphism. For $x\in\mathbb C$ and $r>0$, put $L(x,r)=\max_{|y-x|=r}|h(y)-h(x)|$ and $l(x,r)=\min_{|y-x|=r}|h(y)-h(x)|$. Suppose $L(x,r)\le H l(x,r)$ for every $x,r$, with one fixed $1\le H<\infty$. Then $h\in W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, its continuous representative is ACL, and it is analytically $H$-quasiconformal:
$$|h_{\bar z}|\le\frac{H-1}{H+1}|h_z|\quad\hbox{almost everywhere}.$$
For relatively compact open sets $V\Subset U\Subset\mathbb C$, a coordinate unit vector $e_i$ and $0<|t|<\operatorname{dist}(V,\partial U)/2$, one has the explicit estimate
$$\int_V\left|\frac{h(x+te_i)-h(x)}t\right|^2\,dx\le4H^2\operatorname{area}(h(U)).$$

items.title: Lobachevsky Fourier expansion and a certified π/3 value
items.statement:
For every real $\theta$, $\Lambda$ is continuous, odd, and $\pi$-periodic, with $\Lambda(\pi/2)=0$ and
$$\Lambda(2\theta)=2\Lambda(\theta)+2\Lambda(\theta+\pi/2).$$
For $0\le\theta\le\pi$,
$$\Lambda(\theta)=\frac12\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{\sin(2n\theta)}{n^2}.$$
In particular,
$$\Lambda(\pi/3)=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \left(\frac1{(3k+1)^2}-\frac1{(3k+2)^2}\right).$$
For every integer $N\ge1$, the positive remainder after the terms $k=0,\ldots,N$ is at most $\sqrt3/(72N^2)$.

items.title: Shape parameters of an ideal tetrahedron
items.statement: For an oriented ideal tetrahedron with normalized vertices $0,1,\infty,z$ and $\operatorname{Im}z>0$, its three edge-shape parameters are $z$, $z'=1/(1-z)$, and $z''=(z-1)/z$. They satisfy $zz'z''=-1$, and their arguments in $(0,\pi)$ are the three dihedral angles, whose sum is $\pi$. For $\omega=e^{i\pi/3}$, the choice $z=\omega$ gives $z=z'=z''=\omega$ and all six dihedral angles equal to $\pi/3$.

items.title: A rank-two horocusp truncation has finite volume
items.statement:
Let $\Gamma\subset\mathbb C$ be a rank-two lattice acting on $\mathbb H^3$ by horizontal translations, and let
$$
C=\{(x+iy,t):t\ge1\}/\Gamma
$$
be the quotient of the horoball $t\ge1$. If $A$ is the Euclidean area of a fundamental parallelogram for $\Gamma$, then the end is at infinite hyperbolic distance and $\operatorname{Vol}(C)=A/2$.

references.title: Jessica S. Purcell, Hyperbolic Knot Theory
references.locator: §4.3, cusp neighborhoods and completeness equations, printed pp.73–77

items.title: Group isomorphisms of standard cusped hyperbolic manifolds give equivariant quasi-isometries

references.title: Gopal Prasad, Strong Rigidity of Q-Rank 1 Lattices
references.locator: Theorem C and its proof; the ordinary torus-cusp construction needed here is given directly, without the reductive cusp-base machinery

items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $M=\Gamma\backslash\mathbb H^3$ and $N=\Gamma'\backslash\mathbb H^3$ be connected orientable hyperbolic manifolds, with discrete torsion-free groups. Suppose each is a compact core together with finitely many disjoint standard torus cusp ends: an end is an embedded quotient $\{y>R_i\}/\Lambda_i$ by a rank-two translation lattice, and the complement of the union of these ends is compact. Zero ends are allowed, in which case the manifold is compact.

Every group isomorphism $\theta:\Gamma\to\Gamma'$ permutes the conjugacy classes of the peripheral cusp groups. There is a smooth $\theta$-equivariant quasi-isometry $F:\mathbb H^3\to\mathbb H^3$ which on every sufficiently deep lifted cusp is affine in its horizontal coordinates and preserves cusp depth after a constant height rescaling. It has a smooth equivariant quasi-inverse with inverse affine cusp maps. On quotient manifolds these maps are proper homotopy equivalences.

The standard cusp decomposition is a supplied hypothesis here; this lemma does not derive it merely from finite volume.

items.title: A quasi-isometry of hyperbolic three-space has a quasiconformal boundary map

references.title: Gopal Prasad, Strong Rigidity of Q-Rank 1 Lattices
references.locator: Printed pp. 256–257 and Theorem C; the specialized passage from a quasi-isometry to a quasiconformal sphere map is proved independently here

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. On $\mathbb H^3=\{(z,s):z\in\mathbb C,\ s>0\}$ use the metric $s^{-2}(|dz|^2+ds^2)$. Suppose $f:\mathbb H^3\to\mathbb H^3$ is a quasi-isometry with constants $\lambda\ge1$, $\varepsilon\ge0$:
$$\lambda^{-1}d(x,y)-\varepsilon\le d(f(x),f(y))\le\lambda d(x,y)+\varepsilon,$$
and with coarsely dense image. Then it induces an ideal-boundary homeomorphism $h:\widehat{\mathbb C}\to\widehat{\mathbb C}$. There is $H=H(\lambda,\varepsilon)<\infty$ such that, after postcomposition by any Möbius transformation carrying $h(\infty)$ to $\infty$, its plane restriction satisfies
$$\max_{|a-z|=r}|h(a)-h(z)|\le H\min_{|a-z|=r}|h(a)-h(z)|\qquad(z\in\mathbb C,\ r>0).$$
Here $h$ in that inequality denotes the normalized map. If the boundary homeomorphism preserves orientation, it is analytically quasiconformal in sphere charts, with constant at most $H$. If it reverses orientation, postcomposition with complex conjugation is quasiconformal with that constant. If $f$ is equivariant for a homomorphism between groups of hyperbolic isometries, its boundary map is equivariant for their boundary actions.

items.title: Cusp multipliers detect completeness
items.statement: Let an orientable finite ideal triangulation have exactly one ideal vertex, whose link is a torus. Suppose its tetrahedra carry positive shapes whose edge products equal $1$ and whose dihedral angles sum to $2\pi$ around every edge. If the cusp multipliers $H(\alpha)$ and $H(\beta)$ are $1$ for a basis $\alpha,\beta$ of the torus fundamental group, then the glued hyperbolic metric is complete at that cusp.

items.title: Volume of an ideal orthoscheme region
items.statement:
For $0<\zeta<\pi/2$, let
$$\mathcal O_\zeta= \{(x+iy,t)\in\mathbb H^3: 0\le x\le\cos\zeta,\quad 0\le y\le x\tan\zeta,\quad t\ge\sqrt{1-x^2-y^2}\}.$$
Its hyperbolic volume in the upper half-space metric is $\frac12\Lambda(\zeta)$.

items.statement: Assume AC. Every nonempty connected oriented complete Riemannian three-manifold of constant sectional curvature $-1$ is isometric to $\Gamma\backslash\mathbb H^3$ for a discrete torsion-free subgroup $\Gamma\le\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb C)$. The covering is a universal Riemannian covering and identifies $\Gamma$ with the fundamental group up to the usual basepoint conjugacies. Its completeness and quotient presentation are conclusions from the stated metric hypotheses. The orientation-preserving isometry group of the model is $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb C)$ with its usual Möbius boundary action.

items.title: Volume of the regular ideal tetrahedron
items.statement:
Every regular ideal tetrahedron in hyperbolic three-space has volume
$$v_3=3\Lambda(\pi/3) =\frac{3\sqrt3}{4}\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \left(\frac1{(3k+1)^2}-\frac1{(3k+2)^2}\right).$$

items.statement: Assume AC. Let $M$ be a nonempty connected oriented complete Riemannian three-manifold of constant curvature $-1$ and finite volume. Then $M$ is a compact core together with finitely many pairwise disjoint standard torus cusp ends. Each end is an embedded quotient $\{y>R_i\}/\Lambda_i$ of a horoball by a rank-two translation lattice, and the complement of these open ends is compact. The number of cusps may be zero. In particular, the standard cusp decomposition in the general rigidity construction follows from the complete finite-volume metric, with no knot or triangulation assumption.

items.title: Pared hyperbolic structures and volume
items.statement:
A compact orientable three-manifold $M$ is **irreducible** if every embedded $2$-sphere in its interior bounds an embedded $3$-ball in $M$. A properly embedded surface is **incompressible** if it admits no embedded disk whose interior misses the surface and whose boundary is an essential simple closed curve in it. A boundary subsurface is **$\pi_1$-injective** if the inclusion of each component induces an injection on fundamental groups. A **pared pair** is a pair $(M,P)$ in which $M$ is compact, orientable and irreducible, and $P$ is a possibly empty compact subsurface of $\partial M$ whose pairwise disjoint components are $\pi_1$-injective annuli or tori, every noncyclic abelian subgroup of $\pi_1(M)$ is conjugate into $\pi_1$ of a component of $P$ up to base-path conjugacy, and every map of pairs
$$
(S^1\times I,S^1\times\partial I)\longrightarrow(M,P)
$$
that induces injections on fundamental groups is homotopic through maps of pairs into $P$, so its boundary remains in $P$ during the homotopy. Write $\partial_0M=\partial M\setminus\operatorname{int}P$. A **horoball** is a region bounded by a horosphere, a Euclidean plane or sphere tangent to the ideal boundary at one point. The **peripheral subgroup** for a component of $P$ is the image of its fundamental group in $\pi_1(M)$, recorded up to conjugacy. A **hyperbolic structure** on $(M,P)$ is a curvature $-1$ metric on $\operatorname{int}M$ described by an atlas of charts into $\mathbb H^3$ whose transition maps are in $\operatorname{Isom}^+(\mathbb H^3)$. Its developing map $\operatorname{dev}$ from the universal cover and holonomy homomorphism $\rho:\pi_1(M)\to\operatorname{Isom}^+(\mathbb H^3)$ satisfy $\operatorname{dev}(gx)=\rho(g)\operatorname{dev}(x)$. The metric is **complete** when it is geodesically complete. A **cusp** corresponding to a component of $P$ is a quotient of a horoball by the associated peripheral subgroup. The hyperbolic volume is the integral of the Riemannian volume density over $\operatorname{int}M$; the structure has **finite volume** when this integral is finite.

items.title: An isometry preserves the finite hyperbolic volume integral
items.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $M$ and $N$ be second-countable oriented hyperbolic three-manifolds, and let $f:M\to N$ be an isometry. Then
$$
\int_M d\operatorname{vol}_M=\int_N d\operatorname{vol}_N.
$$
In particular, if either volume is finite, then both are finite and the values agree.

items.title: Finite-volume hyperbolic knot exterior
items.statement: For a smooth knot $K$ with chosen compact exterior $E_K$ and boundary torus $T_K$, a finite-volume hyperbolic knot exterior structure is a complete Riemannian metric of constant sectional curvature $-1$ on $\operatorname{int}(E_K)$ with finite volume and exactly one cusp whose torus cross-section is isotopic in $\operatorname{int}(E_K)$ to a parallel copy of $T_K$. The definition asserts no existence.

items.title: Nontrivial knot exteriors are irreducible and boundary-incompressible
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K:S^1\to S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with a chosen product tubular neighbourhood $N(K)$, and set $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ and $T_K=\partial E_K$. If $K$ is not ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms to the standard unknot, then every smoothly embedded $2$-sphere in $\operatorname{int}E_K$ bounds an embedded $3$-ball in $E_K$, and there is no smoothly embedded disk $D\subset E_K$ whose interior misses $T_K$ and whose boundary is an essential simple closed curve in $T_K$.

items.title: Thurston hyperbolization for atoroidal knot exteriors
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $E_K$ be the compact connected orientable exterior of a smooth knot in $S^3$, with one torus boundary component. If $E_K$ is irreducible, its boundary is incompressible, $E_K$ is atoroidal, and $E_K$ is not Seifert-fibered, then $\operatorname{int}(E_K)$ admits a complete finite-volume Riemannian metric of constant sectional curvature $-1$ with one torus cusp. No conclusion is asserted for a torus or satellite knot unless its exterior satisfies all four topological hypotheses.

items.title: The standard two-tetrahedron figure-eight gluing is complete
items.statement:
Define the standard figure-eight knot $K_8$ to be the oriented closure of the three-strand geometric braid $(\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^2$. Its endpoint permutation is a $3$-cycle, so this closure has one component.

Let $\Delta_0=[0,1,2,3]$ and $\Delta_1=[0',1',2',3']$ be oriented ideal tetrahedra with orientation-reversing affine face maps
$$[0,1,2]\to[3',1',2'],\quad [0,1,3]\to[0',1',2'],\quad [0,2,3]\to[0',1',3'],\quad [1,2,3]\to[0',2',3'].$$
This is the two-tetrahedron ideal triangulation obtained from the standard four-crossing figure-eight diagram by cutting along crossing arcs, identifying upper and lower polyhedron faces with equal region labels, and collapsing the two bigon faces. Its edge classes are
$$\{01,02,23,0'1',1'3',2'3'\},\qquad \{12,03,13,1'2',0'2',0'3'\};$$
each has valence six, and the unique ideal vertex link is a torus. Put shape $z_1$ on $01,23$, shape $z_2$ on $03,12$, and shape $z_3$ on $02,13$ in $\Delta_0$; put shape $w_1$ on $0'1',2'3'$, shape $w_2$ on $0'3',1'2'$, and shape $w_3$ on $0'2',1'3'$ in $\Delta_1$. Unfold the eight cusp-link triangles by the face maps into the standard rectangular strip. Its upper-row labels are $a,b,c,d$ and its lower-row labels are $h,g,f,e$, both read from left to right; the corner trace across the strip is therefore $a,h,b,g,c,f,d,e$. Identify the strip boundary sides as prescribed by those same maps. Let $\alpha$ be the edge path across the strip from the left side of $a$ on the left boundary to the left side of $a$ on the right boundary, and let $\beta$ be the edge path on the left boundary from the base of $a$ to the top of $h$. Their ordered corner factors are respectively $z_3,w_2^{-1},z_2,w_3^{-1},z_3,w_2^{-1},z_2,w_3^{-1}$ and $z_2^{-1},w_1$. The face-pairing incidence check gives one positive transverse intersection, so their homology classes form a basis of $H_1$ and the loops form a basis of $\pi_1$ of the torus link. The two edge products are $z_1^2z_3w_1^2w_3$ and $z_2^2z_3w_2^2w_3$, while
$$H(\alpha)=\left(\frac{z_2z_3}{w_2w_3}\right)^2,\qquad H(\beta)=\frac{w_1}{z_2}.$$
For $\omega=e^{i\pi/3}$, assigning $z_1=z_2=z_3=w_1=w_2=w_3=\omega$ makes both edge products and both cusp multipliers equal to $1$ and gives total angle $2\pi$ around each edge. The gluing therefore gives the figure-eight complement a complete finite-volume curvature $-1$ metric with one peripheral torus cusp.

items.statement: Assume AC. Let $M$ and $N$ be nonempty connected oriented complete finite-volume Riemannian three-manifolds of constant curvature $-1$. There is no knot, compactness, or cusp-number restriction. Every isomorphism $\theta:\pi_1(M)\to\pi_1(N)$, up to conjugacy from basepoint changes, is induced by a unique isometry $I:M\to N$. The isometry is properly homotopic to every proper homotopy equivalence inducing that outer isomorphism. Its orientation agrees with that of such an equivalence, and the two Riemannian volumes are equal.

items.title: Atoroidal non-Seifert knot exteriors have the required topological hypotheses
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth knot in $S^3$ that is not ambient isotopic to the standard unknot, and assume its compact exterior $E_K$ is atoroidal and not Seifert-fibered. Then every smoothly embedded $2$-sphere in $\operatorname{int}E_K$ bounds an embedded $3$-ball in $E_K$, and there is no smoothly embedded disk in $E_K$ whose interior misses $\partial E_K$ and whose boundary is essential in $\partial E_K$.

items.title: Mostow–Prasad rigidity and knot volume
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ and $N$ be interiors of compact connected oriented knot exteriors carrying complete finite-volume hyperbolic metrics. Every isomorphism $\pi_1(M)\to\pi_1(N)$, considered up to the conjugacy induced by basepoint changes, is realized by a unique isometry in the corresponding proper homotopy class. If the isomorphism is induced by an orientation-preserving proper homotopy equivalence, the isometry preserves orientation. In particular, the two metrics have equal volume, where volume is the integral of their Riemannian volume densities.
items.strategy: owner-escalation: a complete local proof must extend the induced quasi-isometry to the sphere at infinity, establish conformal rigidity and cusp control, straighten to an isometry, and then use isometry invariance of the volume integral.

items.title: Worked case: the figure-eight complement
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be the standard figure-eight knot and $E_K$ its compact exterior. Its interior admits a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric obtained by gluing two regular ideal tetrahedra; each edge class has total angle $2\pi$, both generators of the peripheral torus have trivial rotation-and-scale cusp multiplier, and its complete hyperbolic volume is $6\Lambda(\pi/3)=2v_3\approx2.02988$.
